findings.body:
Removal of the `ALLOWED_HOSTS` check (previously performed on `urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).hostname`) means `deliver` now issues an HTTP POST to any URL supplied by the caller.

If a malicious or compromised caller passes an external or internal target URL, the service will send the event payload there. This is a classic SSRF / data-exfiltration risk.

```suggestion
    host = urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).hostname or ""
    if host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS:
        raise ValueError("webhook host not allowed")
```

summary: The change removes the only host-authorization guard in the webhook delivery path. The previous implementation rejected any URL whose hostname was not in `ALLOWED_HOSTS`; the new version performs an unconditional `urllib.request.urlopen` to whatever URL the caller supplies. This introduces a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vector and allows arbitrary event data to be exfiltrated to attacker-controlled endpoints. No compensating controls (scheme validation, private-IP blocking, redirect following limits, or caller-side authorization) are present in the diff or the surrounding file.

verification.reason: Base `webhooks.py` restricted POSTs to `ALLOWED_HOSTS` via `urlsplit(url).hostname`; head removes that check and posts the event to any caller-supplied URL, which is a real SSRF/exfiltration regression.
